中胡是二十世紀四十年代在中國發展而成的拉弦樂器，屬於胡琴家族的重要成員。它的創製: The zhonghu is a bowed string instrument developed in China in the 1940s and an important member of the huqin family. It was created out of musicians' wish to enrich the tonal layers of the national orchestra, filling the gap in range between the gaohu and the erhu. Its timbre is low and full, between the erhu and the bass huqin, and it opened new possibilities for traditional ensemble playing.
中胡為中國弓弦樂器，屬弦鳴，發聲原理與二胡相近。來源指出它與二胡、高胡同屬胡琴家: The zhonghu is a Chinese bowed instrument, a chordophone, and it makes sound much as the erhu does. The source notes that it belongs with the erhu and gaohu to the huqin family and has added a middle and lower register to Chinese orchestras; as for listening, it can be confirmed in the line-up of Chinese orchestras. The composer Jeremy Zuckerman also used the zhonghu in the music of a well-received programme, and used it together with the erhu in the music for that programme's final episode. The source gives no specific piece titles, so none are listed.
中胡的琴筒多採用紫檀木或楠木等優質硬木製造，具有良好的共鳴特性。琴桿與琴頭通常由: The zhonghu's soundbox is usually made from good hardwood such as rosewood or nanmu, which resonates well. The neck and head are usually of mahogany or ebony. The head skin is python or sheepskin, carefully treated to vibrate best. The bow stick is bamboo, the bow hair horsehair. The strings are steel or silk, and metal fittings such as fine tuners and tuning pegs are copper or stainless steel, for durability and stable tone.
中胡音色深沉而溫潤，具有渾厚的質感，介於高胡的明亮與低胡的厚重之間。其音域位於中: The zhonghu's timbre is deep and warm, with a full body, sitting between the brightness of the gaohu and the heaviness of the bass huqin. Its range lies in the middle, and it can play both warm, gentle melodies and forceful notes with tension. The design of its soundbox lets it produce warm overtones, and it is fuller in volume than the erhu. Next to the sharp brightness of the gaohu it sounds calm and inward; next to the bass huqin it keeps more agility and clarity. Its timbre suits lyrical melodies and folk colour especially well, and in an orchestra it often links the registers, adding a warm middle layer to the overall sound.

The zhonghu (H-S 321.313) is a Chinese bowed instrument of the lower register, also called the alto erhu, and belongs with the erhu and gaohu to the huqin family. Its construction is close to the erhu's but the body is slightly larger, the playing end is covered with snakeskin, and it carries two strings, usually tuned in fifths, either A and E or G and D, and it is played with a bow. In the 1940s it was developed as the alto voice of the huqin family, extending the range of the Chinese orchestra; the composer Jeremy Zuckerman used it in the scores of Avatar: The Last Airbender and The Legend of Korra, and used it together with the erhu in the score of the final episode of The Legend of Korra.

用弓在弦上擦奏，透過弓毛與弦的摩擦力使弦震動。將樂器穩定持於身前。左手負責按弦或: Draw the bow across the string, so that friction between hair and string sets the string vibrating. Hold the instrument steady in front of the body. The left hand stops the string or changes its sounding length to control the pitch; the right hand sets the string vibrating. A string instrument makes sound by passing the string's vibration into a soundbox, which amplifies it. Bow evenly, using the weight of the arm rather than the strength of the wrist.
隨著時代進展，中胡逐漸被納入民族樂隊編制，成為專業樂團的標準配置樂器。它在傳統戲: As time went on the zhonghu was gradually taken into the national orchestra and became standard equipment in professional ensembles. It plays an important part in accompanying traditional opera, in Chinese symphonic music and in modern compositions for Chinese instruments. Its spread began in mainland China and later extended, through cultural exchange, to Hong Kong and Taiwan and then to international stages. Through several generations of players' practice and improvement its technique has been refined, and it has become an indispensable voice in contemporary Chinese instrumental music.
